title: Stroke answer key: the strokes that move the base onto the goal, and how close N strokes can get

description:
The proposal this ticket implements is ai-workspace/reports/stroke-answer-key-proposal-2026-11-02.md; read it first, with the papers it cites.

Goal: an "answer key" for stroke sculpting. Given the base mesh and the goal mesh, move the base onto the goal the way the spherize node moves a mesh onto a sphere, and work out which strokes make that move. The key is a stroke set in the sculptor's own SVG format whose sculpt approaches the goal, plus the curve of how close N strokes can get. It tells us what good looks like, separates tool limits (base, stroke engine) from sculptor skill, gives the judge spatial feedback to put in words, and grades MESH-90's picture-computed strokes stroke by stroke.

Method (a judge-side Java route, `stroke-key`, with an ixdar-cli command that only calls it):
1. Align base and goal with the normalisation `mesh-compare --normalize` uses.
2. Project (the spherize step): refine the base as a sculpt pass does (StrokeRefinement); from every vertex cast its normal both ways onto the goal (TriangleBvh.nearestHit) for a signed offset h(v). Where the ray misses or meets a back face, fall back to the nearest goal point and mark the vertex unreachable along the normal (deep sockets, under the zygomatic arch).
3. Candidates from h at several scales (scale-space blob detection): regions below -t as sunk fills (FillStroke bowl weights from h), regions above +t as raised fills, crest lines of h (CrestLineDetector / Ohtake ridge-valley lines) as ridge and valley chains with radius from the feature's width and depth from h, silhouette strokes where the base's outline in a template view misses the goal's.
4. Greedy selection (matching pursuit): score candidates with StrokeSculpt itself, never an approximation of its kernel, so the key obeys every limit the sculptor faces; keep the one that lowers the residual most, repeat.
5. Every K strokes refine radius, depth and point positions by coordinate descent; end with a pass that drops strokes whose removal costs nothing.
6. Write the strokes into the 8-cell template SVG, each in the cell that sees it most squarely, in <g id> groups, run through sculpt-sync, so it is the same object a sculptor produces.

Secrecy: the key is the goal in stroke form. Read the goal from ~/.cache/ixdar-sculpt-judge/skull/Skull.obj and write every output that comes from it (h maps, key SVGs, sculpts, pictures, curves) under ~/.cache/ixdar-sculpt-judge/skull/key-mesh91/, never in the worktree's tmp/ or anywhere a sculptor's worktree can reach. Unit tests use hand-made meshes only.

Inputs: run 4's base is round00_base_mesh88.dsl in the judge directory (also tmp/base.ply in the mesh-90 worktree); run 4's references manifest is references_manifest_mesh88.json there; MESH-90 round 4's computed strokes are in the mesh-90 worktree under tmp/edges_r4/. Reference numbers: run 4's hand sculptor 0.0165 chamfer, measurement floor 0.00216 (scores-mesh88.json).
definition-of-done:
All pictures and numbers under ~/.cache/ixdar-sculpt-judge/skull/key-mesh91/ and named in changes-made:
1. The stroke-key route and its ixdar-cli command, documented.
2. Over run 4's base: the h map and the unreachable-vertex map as multiview pictures.
3. The key's chamfer (mesh-compare --normalize) and picture distance at 25, 50, 100, 200 and 400 strokes, as a table and a curve picture, against run 4's 0.0165 and the 0.00216 floor; with a sentence on how much of the plateau the unreachable vertices (the base) account for and how much the stroke engine.
4. The key's strokes over its own sculpt (strokes_overlay.py from the stroke-sculpt skill) and over run 4's references, plus the key's sculpt multiview beside the goal's.
5. MESH-90 round 4's computed strokes matched against the key by location and kind: precision and recall per view and kind, with a picture of matched and unmatched strokes.
6. Unit tests on hand-made meshes: a sphere with one known dent recovers one fill of about that depth and place; a sphere with one known crease recovers one chain along it; the full suite passes.
testing-plan: Run the new unit tests and the full suite; run stroke-key on run 4's base and Skull.obj at 25-400 strokes; render the pictures into the judge directory; match MESH-90 round 4's strokes against the key.
todos: DONE : Methods over 150 lines added here: StrokeKeyRoute.endpointHandler 247, MeshSmoothing.unfold 170, StrokeKey.compute 155, KeyCandidates.chains 151.
unknowns: Is normal projection enough, or does the plateau come from bad correspondences and need Optimal Step Nonrigid ICP (Amberg 2007)?
changes-made: Candidates (2026-11-02): chains offered once at the crease's width (refinement tries narrower and wider) and a piece repeating one already offered (the same crease at a coarser smoothing scale) dropped; fills whose hull spans ground the region does not cover are not offered. 578 candidates became 144 (423 valleys to 53, 55 ridges to 9, 100 fills to 82); the 25-stroke key's chamfer went from 0.01397 to 0.01193, run time 31.5 s to 23.8 s. The route writes candidates.svg (every candidate offered, by layer). Pictures in ~/.cache/ixdar-sculpt-judge/skull/key-mesh91/pictures/candidates_on_base.png, candidates2_on_base.png, key2_025_strokes_on_sculpt.png.

2026-11-04: MESH-89 and MESH-90 combined into this worktree (mesh-90's diff holds all of mesh-89's). mesh-91 synced onto master d76fb8e4, mesh-90's files copied in, the three sculpt files both changed (DisplacementSum, FillStroke, StrokeSculpt) three-way merged; one real overlap, the unfold call, keeps MESH-89's per-stroke fold counting. Probes removed (MeshSmoothing.PROBE_LOG, StrokeSculpt.probeDump, ixdar.probe.* switches, FitProbeTest moved out of the worktree). Consolidation: EdgeDistances and MeshSmoothing.ramp now run on numeric.graph.Dijkstra (a search costs what it settles, no per-call fills of vertex-bound arrays); StrokeChain.snap uses NearestVertex instead of a scan of every vertex per point; MeshTopology.packedPositions replaces StrokeSculpt.packedPositions, MeshDistance.extractPositions and inline copies in MeshSmoothing, NearestVertex, SubdivisionMeshNode; MeshVertexOffset.atPositions builds from absolute positions, so apply's symmetrise and unfold steps and DisplacementSum.sculpted no longer subtract-then-offset (two fewer mesh rebuilds per symmetric pass); numeric.DenseLinearSystem replaces SkeletonSensitivityAnalyzer.solveLinearSystem (ImplicitFit, OffsetCrests, the analyzer); representation.TriangleSoup.edgeFaces/oneRings replace four edge-to-faces loops (SemanticPatchDecomposer, MorseSmaleDecomposer x2, BoundarySnap) and two triangle one-ring builders (BoundarySnap, MscCellAssembly), same HashSet capacity so iteration order is unchanged; MorseSmaleComplex uses PrincipalDirectionField.oneRings; EdgeDihedrals.vertexNormals replaces the copies in SemanticPatchDecomposer and PrincipalDirectionField; SemanticPatchDecomposer uses TriangleGeometry.area. Full suite: 793 of 794 pass, the one failure StrokeKeyTest.oneKnownCreaseComesBackAsOneChainAlongIt, failing before the merge too (a bowl fill wins over the chain since the OffsetCrests change); ixdar_automation_cli test_cli 125 OK.

Profile 2026-11-04 (async-profiler, 3 sculpt passes of the 203-stroke key_050 over run 4's base, ~17 s each warm; profiles in the session scratchpad): sculpt thread wall time refine 30% (requireEdgeLengths tests every vertex in a stroke's box against every stroke point: 60% of refine), stroke sum ~40% (FillStroke.kernel loops every sample per gathered vertex: 26% of all CPU, elementFraction 16% self), MeshFolds.update 14% serial (four full-mesh fold passes per pass: two for the per-stroke counts, unfold's own MeshFolds, half its time in HalfEdgeMesh IntIdTable lookups), unfold edge rays 16% CPU (parallel), TriangleBvh.refit 4%.

Mesh geometry queries shared and cached: MeshTopology gains boundsDiagonal(), signedVolume() and vertexAreas() defaults (radius() javadoc corrected: it is the bounding-sphere radius about the box centre, not half the diagonal). HalfEdgeMesh.vertexPositions is now private; writes go through setVertexPosition / setPositionsById or the vertex and face slot methods, all of which advance a geometryVersion, and the bounds, radius, signed volume and vertex areas are cached against it (volatile version written after the value, safe for the parallel sculpt readers). ArrayMesh caches volume and areas like its bounds. Removed HalfEdgeMesh.computeBoundingBoxDiagonal / computeBoundingSphereRadius. Callers switched: GoalProjection, SurfaceCreases, SemanticPatchDecomposer, SculptSync, MorseSmaleDecomposer, SeamlessParameterization, CurvatureConstraints, ValidateDsl, StrokeKeyRoute, MidpointSplit, HalfEdgeMeshOps; test copies of signed volume removed (RingRegionExtractionTest/Benchmark, MeshBooleanProvenanceTest, which now checks the sign). Full suite 793/794, only the pre-existing crease failure.

One-ring and id-map consolidation: MeshTopology gains activeIndexById() (dense index by vertex id, NONE for dead ids) and oneRings() (dense neighbours across the mesh's own edges). OffsetCrests.rings deleted (KeyCandidates and OffsetCrests use surface.oneRings()). activeIndexById replaces the hand-built maps in DisplacementSum (which packed positions just for the map), MeshLargestPart, MeshVertexOffset, RingRegionExtraction and DungeonGrids; InputShortestEdgePathsNode keeps its own because it refuses sparse ids. PrincipalDirectionField.oneRings deleted: it and CrestLineDetector, SaddlePointDetector and MorseSmaleComplex now use TriangleSoup.oneRings(ed.triangles(), bound), the same triangle-edge neighbour sets in HashSet order rather than edge-map order. Curvature rings stay triangle-based (quad diagonals count as neighbours there), unlike oneRings(). MorseSmaleComplex.buildOrderedOneRing (cyclic, null on open fans) kept. Full suite 793/794, only the pre-existing crease failure.
Secrecy guards dropped from scope: the user keeps the goal model out of the sculptor's worktree instead, so no route needs to refuse writes inside a worktree.

DenseLinearSystem is now a dense Cholesky: a pivot no larger than CholeskyBackend.diagonalShiftFor's shift retries the factorisation with that shift on the diagonal, the sparse solver's policy, and a pivot still below it zeroes that unknown (as the old pivoting did). SkeletonSensitivityAnalyzer's J^T J + lambda I step now goes through DirectSolver/CholeskyBackend (NormalMatrix, NATURAL ordering) like ImplicitFit's level solve. Triangle areas: MeshTopology.faceArea (fan triangles, any polygon) replaces HalfEdgeMesh's triangle-only float faceArea and the inline copies in RingRegions and LayoutPatchMaps; RingCandidateExtractor uses TriangleGeometry.area. MeshHoleFiller (loop held as separate x/y/z arrays) and NDirectionField (area from edge vectors it already builds) keep theirs. SemanticPatchDecomposer's two comments now say largest axis span, not bounding-sphere diameter. GoalProjection: new ops/MeshProjection casts every point's ray both ways on RayBatch in parallel (was a serial loop); new shrinkwrap node (ShrinkwrapMeshNode, ShrinkwrapMeshNodeTest) projects vertices along their normals onto a target with a kept offset; MeshDistance.normalizedPositions gains a frame mesh and inFrame maps back, used by GoalProjection.moved and project; javadoc no longer says spherize; an unreachable vertex with no nearest goal point now gets offset 0 instead of keeping a back face's distance. Launch entry 'MESH-91: stroke sculpt head' opens dsl/stroke_sculpt_head.dsl in the mesh viewer; screenshot tmp/mesh-91-stroke-sculpt-head.png. Full suite 794/795, only the pre-existing crease failure.

Perf, measured on the key_050 answer-key pass (203 strokes, warm): 17 s before this round, 12.5 s with the stroke element grid, 11.1 s with flat MeshFolds adjacency. (1) New sculpt/StrokeElementGrid buckets a stroke's elements on a grid across its direction, cells one radius wide, each cell listing in index order the elements whose radius-grown box touches it; SculptStroke.requireEdgeLengths, FillStroke.kernel and ChainStroke.kernel visit only the vertex's cell, in the same order, so results are unchanged (elementFraction 30% of CPU to 3%, requireEdgeLengths 28% to 4%). (2) MeshFolds reads each vertex's faces and each face's corners into flat int arrays once at construction instead of HalfEdgeMesh's per-element IntIdList objects on every pass (MeshFolds.update 26% to 12%, IntIdList cache misses 15% to 3%). Full suite 794/795, only the pre-existing crease failure.

Perf correction: count the first pass in a fresh JVM, not warm runs. Cold first pass on key_050 (203 strokes, same harness and CPU profiler): 19.8 s before (one JVM) vs 13.1, 15.3 and 15.1 s after (three JVMs), about a quarter faster. About 16% of cold CPU is inside libjvm (JIT compilation and GC, unsymbolised). The warm figures above (17 to 11.1 s) are not the measure.

Launch entry 'MESH-91: answer key 050' opens ${userHome}/.cache/ixdar-sculpt-judge/skull/key-mesh91/lines50w/key_050.dsl in the mesh viewer (577,667 vertices after the sculpt). ixdar-cli launch now expands ${userHome} and ${env:NAME} as VS Code does (launch_entry.expand_variables, test added); it only knew ${workspaceFolder}, so the headless run read the path as relative to ixdar-app. CLI tests 125/126: test_shutdown_kills_a_process_that_outlives_the_timeout reads the checkout's real tmp/automation and fails while an F5 window is open (the user's, pid 1741078); rerun once it is closed.

Perf, the three work-cutting items. (1) FillStroke.seed asks the pass's vertex grid (StrokeChain.nearestVertex, new NearestVertex.within radius query) for the vertices within each sample's spacing, visited in dense order, instead of testing every vertex in the fill's box per sample; a sample with none within its spacing still scans for its nearest. (2) MeshSmoothing.unfold takes the caller's MeshFolds (new overload); StrokeSculpt passes the one it counts folds with, so a pass builds one fold test, not two. (3) StrokePursuit: each candidate's full move is kept from its first lift, so fold limits are measured from it instead of lifting and summing the stroke again (measureFolds, refineShapes); every worker's DisplacementSum shares one TriangleBvh; pursue keeps each candidate's correlation and after a choice recomputes only candidates whose atoms share a vertex with the chosen one (vertex-to-candidate index built once per call). Also moved StrokePursuit's orphaned correlate javadoc. Outputs unchanged: sculpt tests give the same crease numbers; a pursuit probe on StrokeKeyTest's dent and crease goals prints identical strokes, depths and residuals before and after. Cold first sculpt pass on key_050: 11.5, 11.5 and 13.2 s in three fresh JVMs (19.8 s at the start of the perf work). Key-building (pursuit) time on the skull not yet measured: the user's F5 window was open in the worktree and the route would have run in it. Full suite 794/795, only the pre-existing crease failure.

Key-building timing on the skull (stroke-key --counts 50 --symmetry x --ridge-levels 6 --goal-line-radius 0.04, into key-mesh91/perf-check): 24.1 s against the judge's lines50w run's 45.0 s, but not like for like: this run offered 798 candidates (1,352 atoms, 216 strokes) to that run's 612 (1,134, 203), so its parameters or candidate code differ. By stage, then vs now: candidate atoms 4.7 vs 2.9 s, pursue 2.8 vs 1.1, sweep depths 0.5 vs 0.2, refine shapes 8.4 vs 2.2, prune and fresh fills 5.9 vs 6.4, sculpt pass 20.7 vs 9.8 (the pass runs after the pursuit in the same JVM, so it is partly warm).

Crease case fixed. Cause: OffsetCrests set each chain's radius to 2 sqrt(|d| / |f''|) from the smoothed offset field, and both the two-ring quadratic fit (which flattens a narrow peak) and the smoothing inflate it: the test's groove of radius 0.12 was offered as a chain of radius 0.239, too wide to beat a bowl fill (0.000308 vs 0.000312 explained). New OffsetCrests.fittedWidth fits the width to the unsmoothed offsets around the line instead: the bump d (1 - (s / w)^2)^2 with d in closed form, w by golden-section search up to 1.5 times that estimate; the crease's chain is now 0.143 wide and is chosen. The goal-line branch of KeyCandidates.chains uses the same fit, capped at half the gap to the nearest other line (its old width), so goal-line widths can only narrow. StrokeKeyTest passes; full suite 795/795; CLI tests 126/126. Long methods: StrokeKey.compute (goal lines mapped by MeshDistance.normalized + inFrame, new normalized(float[], frame) shared with normalizedPositions) and KeyCandidates.chains (repeated-piece test uses SculptStroke.nearestDistances) are now under 150. StrokeKeyRoute.endpointHandler is 241 (its --out worktree guard removed, the user having dropped secrecy, and the template parsed once) and MeshSmoothing.unfold 169: neither has a repeated piece to share, so they stay until the user decides. ixd wt done: 47 named tests pass, launch entry runs, marked REVIEW.
